Witness: For X = \ell_2^2(\mathbb{C}), Y = \mathbb{C}, and T(z_1, z_2) = \operatorname{Re}(z_1) + i\operatorname{Re}(z_2), \|T\| = 1 but \|T_m\|_{cb} \ge \sqrt{2} > 1. Specifically, for Z_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix} and Z_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \|(Z_1, Z_2)\|_{M_2(\operatorname{Min}_{\mathbb{C}}(X))} = \sqrt{2}, while \|T_2(Z_1, Z_2)\|_{M_2(\mathbb{C})} = \|Z_1 + i Z_2\| = 2$. Thus \|T_m\|_{cb} \neq \|T\| in general, and the proof of Proposition 2.3 (which incorrectly applies the universal property of Min in reverse) as well as its application to deduce that q is completely contractive in [p10-3] fail to hold as stated.

## Proposition 2.3. 
Let T : X → Y be a continuous real linear map between complex Banach spaces, and let T_m be T regarded as a real linear map from Min_C(X) to Min_C(Y). Then ‖T_m‖_cb = ‖T‖.
